### MCPJam Cloud

Account-b
ound commands. Declare `--api-key` / `--api-url` on `mcpjam cloud` (before or after descendants). `mcpjam oauth login` is MCP-serv

er OAuth; `mcpjam cloud login` is your MCPJam account.

| Group | Purpose | Key commands |
| - | - | - |
| [`cloud`](https://d
ocs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-workspace) | Account, project link, and workspace | `login`, `logout`, `whoami`, `link`, `statu
s`, `organizations`, `projects`, `sessions` |\n| [`cloud eval`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-eval-commands) | Autho
r and run eval suites in your hosted MCPJam projects | `create`, `list`, `run`, `status` |\n| [`cloud tunnel`](https://docs.mcpjam
.com/cli/reference#cloud-tunnel) | Expose a local MCP server through a public MCPJam tunnel URL, registered as a server in your pr
oject | `tunnel --server <name> <url>`, `tunnel --server <name> -- <command>` |\n| [`cloud clients`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/r
eference#cloud-clients-commands) | Manage clients in your hosted MCPJam projects (`cloud hosts` is a deprecated alias) | `list`, `
get`, `create`, `update`, `servers`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `templates` |\n| [`cloud environments`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/re
ference#cloud-environments-commands) | Manage project environments — the host + servers + pinned skills/plugins bundles eval suite
s and goals run against | `list`, `get`, `resolve`, `create`, `update`, `archive`, `restore` |\n| [`cloud images`](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-images-commands) | Manage custom Computer sandbox images (blueprints) | `list`, `get`, `create`, `val
idate`, `edit`, `build`, `logs`, `use`, `reset`, `promote`, `delete` |\n| [`cloud skills`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#c
loud-skills-commands) | List and read Cloud Skills in your hosted MCPJam projects — discover the skill IDs that `--compose-skill`
and `--skill` require (read-only; authoring is in the app) | `list`, `get` |\n| [`cloud projects servers`](https://docs.mcpjam.com
/cli/reference#cloud-projects-servers-commands) | Connect MCP servers to a project and manage pending connection requests | `conne
ct`, `connect-status`, `connect-cancel` |\n\nAlso under `mcpjam cloud`: `goals` (`journeys` is a deprecated alias), `personas`, `s
warms`, and `studies` (which publishes an environment for outside testers and reads what they did; `scenarios` and `user-testing`
are deprecated aliases for it). Full flag tables are in the [command reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md).\n\n## C
loud credentials and API URL\n\n`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or after descendants (`
mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands, including hosted
`readiness`, reject those flags at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.\n\nCredential precedence fo

r Cloud commands:

1. `--api-key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same
`sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth fr
om `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` r

eports `missing` instead)

API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server wit
hout `/api/v1`)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins rec
orded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)\n4. `ht
tps://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`\n\nEvery command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its
server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an
`http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables namin
g different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved l
ogin is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before an
y request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: f
alse`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are information
al (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud a
s … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.\n\

n## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in

`--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most recently updated p
roject you can see\n\nEmpty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI

project (it is SDK eval reporting only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpjam cloud link
# writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: credential, deploymen

t, selector
mcpjam cloud eval list # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval` run-inspec
tion commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) follow the s
ame rule — `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-project listing and c

annot be combined with `--project`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means

`--host` is not

one flag. The meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `resources`, `prompt
s` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, and protocol versi
on in `initialize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, tool visibility an
d model settings. Never the real client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default is all. |\n| `clou
